steps.title: Abruzzo and the Marche
steps.body: Montepulciano dominates Abruzzo, between the Apennines and the Adriatic. It's also important in the Marche, Molise and Puglia. In Abruzzo, the hills between mountains and sea give warm days and cool breezes. Vines are often trained on high pergolas, called tendone, which shade the fruit.

steps.title: Late and warm
steps.body: Montepulciano ripens late and needs warmth; in cooler years it can taste green and harsh. That's why it's rarely grown further north. Its thick skins give deep colour and resist disease. High yields are possible, so quality depends on controlling them.

steps.prompt: Match each wine to its region.
steps.explanation: Montepulciano anchors the Adriatic side of central Italy.

steps.body: In Abruzzo, look for Colline Teramane, a DOCG zone in the north of the region, for more structured Montepulciano.

steps.prompt: Why is Montepulciano rarely grown in northern Italy?
options: It ripens late and needs warmth
steps.explanation: Cool climates leave it unripe and harsh.
